=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1205-1235 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `filter_runtime_status_noise` suppresses `.serena/` status lines broadly enough to hide legitimate Codex-created `.serena/` changes.
  WHY: Multiple reviews reported that the hash-gated case pattern can make real `.serena/` work look like no-op and cause false delta detection; deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro disputed that this is a bug.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2492-2504 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The `rm -rf .serena` cleanup can delete legitimate Codex-created files under `.serena/` before staging.
  WHY: Multiple reviews reported that the hash-gated cleanup removes the whole directory, so any non-bootstrap `.serena/` contents are lost; deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro disputed that this is a bug.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:98-148 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The inline Python helper reads `sys.argv[1]` and `sys.argv[2]` without validating its argument count.
  WHY: Several reviews noted the helper can raise `IndexError` on malformed invocation even though the current shell caller passes both arguments.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2017-2018 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The same inline Python helper pattern in the repair path reads `sys.argv[1]` and `sys.argv[2]` without validating its argument count.
  WHY: minimax_minimax-m2_5 reported the same defensive gap in the repair helper and noted it would raise `IndexError` on malformed invocation.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1196-1305 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The Serena regression test checks workflow text patterns but does not execute a `.serena/` mutation scenario.
  WHY: Several reviews said the test can pass even if runtime filtering/cleanup still drops real `.serena/` changes because it is structural rather than behavioral.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1140 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The regex assertion is overly specific because it pins the exact string in the test.
  WHY: deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro described this as an intended contract test with minor maintenance overhead rather than a defect.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1217-1659 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `filter_runtime_status_noise` may not be available inside pipeline subshells.
  WHY: deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro reported the concern but concluded Bash function inheritance makes it work correctly, so it was judged not a real issue.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1217 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `.serena/` status filtering can suppress legitimate Codex changes under `.serena/`.
  WHY: Deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro disagreed, arguing the bootstrap-hash gate means `.serena/` entries are intentionally treated as runtime state and not a bug.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1217-1659 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `filter_runtime_status_noise` may not be available inside pipeline subshells.
  WHY: Deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro concluded Bash function inheritance covers the call sites, so this was not a real issue.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2495-2500 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `rm -rf .serena` cleanup can delete Codex modifications under `.serena/`.
  WHY: Deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro disagreed, saying the cleanup only fires when the bootstrap hash still matches and that this is intentional runtime-state cleanup.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:101 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Python helper lacks an argument-count check before reading `sys.argv[1]` and `sys.argv[2]`.
  WHY: Deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro disagreed, noting the shell caller always passes both arguments so an `IndexError` is not realistic.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1140 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The regex assertion is overly specific about the exact string.
  WHY: Deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro treated this as an intended contract test with minor maintenance overhead, not a defect.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1249 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test does not exercise a `.serena/` mutation scenario.
  WHY: Deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro acknowledged the gap but said the suite is intentionally contract-based rather than behavioral.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1211-1235 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `filter_runtime_status_noise` function filters out all `.serena/` status lines when the bootstrap hash matches.
  WHY: That can hide legitimate Codex-created `.serena/` files and produce false no-op classification.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2492-2500 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The cleanup step deletes the entire `.serena/` directory when only `.serena/project.yml` was bootstrap-owned.
  WHY: That can erase legitimate Codex-created `.serena/` files before commit staging.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:107-108 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Python helper reads `sys.argv[1]` and `sys.argv[2]` without validating that both arguments were passed.
  WHY: A malformed invocation would raise `IndexError` instead of failing with a clearer shell-level error.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2017-2018 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The same Python helper pattern in the repair helper also lacks argument validation.
  WHY: Also present in: .github/workflows/implement.yml lines 2017-2018 (same pattern in repair helper)
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1246-1280 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The regression test verifies text patterns but does not exercise a real `.serena/` mutation scenario.
  WHY: That leaves the runtime filter/cleanup behavior untested even though the bug depends on actual file mutations.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1211-1223 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `.serena/` path filter is overly broad and may hide legitimate changes under `.serena/`.
  WHY: If a repo creates or edits non-`project.yml` files under `.serena/`, those changes can be filtered out when the bootstrap hash matches.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2492-2504 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The cleanup step removes the entire `.serena/` directory.
  WHY: If Codex or Serena created additional `.serena/` files during the run, they can be deleted before staging.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:101-148 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The Python helper lacks an `len(sys.argv)` guard before accessing `sys.argv[1]` and `sys.argv[2]`.
  WHY: It will crash with `IndexError` if ever invoked with too few arguments, even though the current shell wrapper passes both.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1246-1305 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The regression test checks the presence of filter/cleanup text but does not simulate a `.serena/` mutation after bootstrap.
  WHY: A mutation-based test would be needed to prove the runtime behavior is correct.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1211-1233 | severity=high | confidence=4

  WHY: The hash-gated case pattern filters all matching `.serena/` entries, so a real `.serena/` edit can disappear from delta detection.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2498 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The cleanup step can delete legitimate Codex-created `.serena/` files.
  WHY: `rm -rf .serena` removes the entire directory before porcelain status is captured, so any work under `.serena/` is lost.
- scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh:98-148 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The inline Python helper reads `sys.argv[1]` and `sys.argv[2]` without validating argument count.
  WHY: A malformed invocation would raise `IndexError`, though the current shell caller passes both arguments.
- tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py:1246-1305 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test suite does not exercise a runtime scenario where Codex modifies a file under `.serena/`.
  WHY: Static text checks can pass even if the actual filter/cleanup logic still drops real `.serena/` changes.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
